+/-! ## State-dependent closeness -/
+
+/-- Two operators are *close within `δ` on `ψ`* when the state-dependent norm of
+their difference is at most `δ`.  This is the relation written `M ≈_δ N` in
+`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
+def CloseOn {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) (M N : Op ι) : Prop :=
+  ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
+
+namespace CloseOn
+
+variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+variable {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ η : ℝ} {M N P U : Op ι}
+
+/-- Equal operators are close at every nonnegative scale. -/
+theorem of_eq (h : M = N) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) : CloseOn ψ δ M N := by
+  have hzero : applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ = 0 := by
+    rw [h, sub_self, applyOperatorToState_zero_op]
+  rw [CloseOn, hzero, norm_zero]
+  exact hδ
+
+/-- Closeness is symmetric. -/
+theorem symm (h : CloseOn ψ δ M N) : CloseOn ψ δ N M := by
+  have happ : applyOperatorToState (N - M) ψ = -applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ := by
+    rw [show N - M = -(M - N) by abel]
+    unfold applyOperatorToState
+    simp only [map_neg, LinearMap.neg_apply]
+  rw [CloseOn, happ, norm_neg]
+  exact h
+
+/-- Enlarging the scale preserves closeness. -/
+theorem mono (h : CloseOn ψ δ M N) (hδ : δ ≤ η) : CloseOn ψ η M N :=
+  le_trans h hδ
+
+/-- Closeness composes by the triangle inequality. -/
+theorem trans (h₁ : CloseOn ψ δ M N) (h₂ : CloseOn ψ η N P) :
+    CloseOn ψ (δ + η) M P := by
+  have hsplit : M - P = (M - N) + (N - P) := by abel
+  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (M - P) ψ‖
+      = ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ + applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ := by
+        rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_add_op]
+    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ :=
+        norm_add_le _ _
+    _ ≤ δ + η := add_le_add h₁ h₂
+
+/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator preserves closeness. -/
+theorem isometry_mul (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (h : CloseOn ψ δ M N) :
+    CloseOn ψ δ (U * M) (U * N) := by
+  have hsub : U * M - U * N = U * (M - N) := by noncomm_ring
+  rw [CloseOn, hsub, norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul hU]
+  exact h
+
+end CloseOn
+
+/-! ## Sign observables of a projective measurement -/
+
+section SignObs
+
+variable {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+
+/-- The `±1`-valued observable attached to a measurement together with a binary
+relabelling of its answers: an answer labelled `0` carries the eigenvalue `1`
+and an answer labelled `1` carries the eigenvalue `-1`.  For the Magic Square
+these are the cell observables of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
+noncomputable def signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (f : α → ZMod 2) : Op d :=
+  ∑ a, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a
+
+/-- The sign observable is the observable of the binary measurement obtained by
+relabelling the answers. -/
+theorem signObs_eq_obsOf_postprocess (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (f : α → ZMod 2) : signObs M f = obsOf (M.postprocess f) := by
+  classical
+  have hcases : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1 := by decide
+  have key : ∀ a : α, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a =
+      (if f a = 0 then M.effect a else 0) - (if f a = 1 then M.effect a else 0) := by
+    intro a
+    rcases hcases (f a) with h | h <;> rw [h] <;>
+      norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one, neg_one_smul]
+  rw [signObs, obsOf, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter,
+    Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
+  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- Formalization-only: the effects of a projective measurement are mutually
+orthogonal, so two spectral combinations of them multiply coefficientwise. -/
+private theorem sum_smul_effect_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c e : α → ℂ) :
+    (∑ a, c a • M.effect a) * (∑ a, e a • M.effect a) =
+      ∑ a, (c a * e a) • M.effect a := by
+  classical
+  have horth : ∀ a b : α, a ≠ b → M.effect a * M.effect b = 0 := fun a b hab =>
+    mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hM M.sum_le_one hab
+  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+  have hidem : M.effect a * M.effect a = M.effect a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem
+  rw [Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.smul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
+  · rw [Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hidem]
+  · intro b _ hba
+    rw [Matrix.mul_smul, horth a b (Ne.symm hba), smul_zero, smul_zero]
+  · intro ha
+    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement multiply by adding their
+relabellings. -/
+theorem signObs_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
+    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M (fun a => f a + g a) := by
+  rw [signObs, signObs, sum_smul_effect_mul M hM, signObs]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+  rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← bit_sign_add]
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- The sign observable of the zero relabelling is the identity. -/
+theorem signObs_const_zero (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
+    signObs M (fun _ => 0) = 1 := by
+  have hb : ((bitSign (0 : ZMod 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by norm_num [bitSign]
+  rw [signObs]
+  simp only [hb, one_smul]
+  exact M.sum_eq_one
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is an involution. -/
+theorem signObs_mul_self (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
+    signObs M f * signObs M f = 1 := by
+  rw [signObs_mul M hM]
+  have hzero : (fun a => f a + f a) = fun _ : α => (0 : ZMod 2) := by
+    funext a
+    exact (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x + x = 0) (f a)
+  rw [hzero, signObs_const_zero]
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
+theorem signObs_conjTranspose (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
+    (signObs M f)ᴴ = signObs M f := by
+  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, signObs, star_sum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+  rw [star_smul]
+  congr 1
+  · simp
+  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is a binary observable, the
+reflection attached to the relabelling `f`. -/
+theorem isBinaryObservable_signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
+    IsBinaryObservable (signObs M f) :=
+  ⟨signObs_conjTranspose M hM f, signObs_mul_self M hM f⟩
+
+omit [DecidableEq α] in
+/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement commute. -/
+theorem signObs_comm (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
+    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M g * signObs M f := by
+  rw [signObs_mul M hM, signObs_mul M hM]
+  congr 1
+  funext a
+  exact add_comm _ _
+
+end SignObs
+
+/-! ## Deviation of joint spectral combinations on the strategy state -/
+
+section JointDefect
+
+/-- Formalization-only: scalars pass through the second tensor factor. -/
+theorem heteroKron_smul_right {ιA ιB : Type} (c : ℂ) (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
+    heteroKron M (c • N) = c • heteroKron M N := by
+  unfold heteroKron
+  exact Matrix.kronecker_smul c M N
+
+/-- Formalization-only: the tensor placement of two orthogonal projections is an
+orthogonal projection. -/
+private theorem isProj_heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {A : Op ιA} {B : Op ιB}
+    (hA : IsProj A) (hB : IsProj B) : IsProj (heteroKron A B) := by
+  have hAi : A * A = A := hA.isIdempotentElem
+  have hBi : B * B = B := hB.isIdempotentElem
+  have hAs : Aᴴ = A := by
+    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]; exact hA.isSelfAdjoint
+  have hBs : Bᴴ = B := by
+    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]; exact hB.isSelfAdjoint
+  constructor
+  · change heteroKron A B * heteroKron A B = heteroKron A B
+    rw [heteroKron_mul, hAi, hBi]
+  · change star (heteroKron A B) = heteroKron A B
+    rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, heteroKron_conjTranspose, hAs, hBs]
+
+/-- Formalization-only: a real spectral combination of the effects of a
+projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
+private theorem sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose {α d : Type} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c : α → ℝ) :
+    (∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a)ᴴ = ∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a := by
+  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_sum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+  rw [star_smul]
+  congr 1
+  · simp
+  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint
+
+/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a real spectral combination on a
+state is the corresponding real combination of the individual quadratic
+forms. -/
+private theorem re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul {ι γ : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype γ] (r : γ → ℝ) (K : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
+    (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (∑ c, ((r c : ℝ) : ℂ) • K c) ψ)).re =
+      ∑ c, r c * (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (K c) ψ)).re := by
+  rw [applyOperatorToState_sum, inner_sum, Complex.re_sum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_
+  rw [applyOperatorToState_smul, inner_smul_right]
+  simp
+
+variable {G : Game}
+
+/-- Formalization-only: the joint effects of the two players form a projective
+measurement on the composite space when both local measurements are
+projective. -/
+private noncomputable def jointMeasurement (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
+    (y : G.QuestionB) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) (T.ιA × T.ιB) :=
+  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
+    (fun ab => heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2))
+    (fun ab => kronecker_nonneg ((T.A x).pos ab.1) ((T.B y).pos ab.2))
+    (by
+      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+      calc ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
+            heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)
+          = ∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a)
+              (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (T.B y).effect b) := by
+            exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (heteroKron_sum_right _ _).symm
+        _ = heteroKron (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (T.A x).effect a) (1 : Op T.ιB) := by
+            rw [(T.B y).sum_eq_one, heteroKron_sum_left]
+        _ = 1 := by rw [(T.A x).sum_eq_one, heteroKron_one_one])
+
+/-- Formalization-only: the effects of the joint measurement. -/
+private theorem jointMeasurement_effect (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
+    (y : G.QuestionB) (ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) :
+    (jointMeasurement T x y).effect ab =
+      heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2) := rfl
+
+/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a joint effect is the Born weight
+of the corresponding answer pair. -/
+private theorem re_inner_jointMeasurement_effect (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
+    (y : G.QuestionB) (ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) :
+    (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState ((jointMeasurement T x y).effect ab) T.ψ)).re =
+      outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 := rfl
+
+/-- A real spectral combination of the joint effects deviates from zero, in the
+state-dependent norm, by at most the mass of the answer pairs carrying a nonzero
+coefficient, scaled by the squared coefficient bound.  This is the estimate that
+converts each Magic Square rejection mass into an operator bound;
+`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+theorem norm_apply_joint_defect_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
+    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
+    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
+    (coef : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → ℝ) (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop)
+    [DecidableRel E] (hbound : ∀ a b, coef a b ^ 2 ≤ 4)
+    (hsupp : ∀ a b, ¬ E a b → coef a b = 0) :
+    ‖applyOperatorToState
+        (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, ((coef a b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
+          heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
+      4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y E := by
+  classical
+  set J := jointMeasurement T x y with hJ
+  have hJproj : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective J := fun ab =>
+    isProj_heteroKron (hA ab.1) (hB ab.2)
+  have hcollapse : (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, ((coef a b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
+      heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)) =
+      ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab := by
+    rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    rfl
+  have hsa : (∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab)ᴴ =
+      ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab :=
+    sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose J hJproj (fun ab => coef ab.1 ab.2)
+  have hsq : ∀ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
+      ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) =
+        ((coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
+    intro ab
+    rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, sq]
+  rw [hcollapse, norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, hsa,
+    sum_smul_effect_mul J hJproj]
+  simp only [hsq]
+  rw [re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul]
+  have hterm : ∀ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
+      coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 *
+          (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState (J.effect ab) T.ψ)).re ≤
+        (if E ab.1 ab.2 then 4 * outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 else 0) := by
+    intro ab
+    have hw : 0 ≤ outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 := outcomeWeight_nonneg T x y ab.1 ab.2
+    rw [re_inner_jointMeasurement_effect]
+    by_cases hE : E ab.1 ab.2
+    · rw [if_pos hE]
+      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hbound ab.1 ab.2) hw
+    · rw [if_neg hE, hsupp ab.1 ab.2 hE]
+      simp
+  calc ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 *
+        (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState (J.effect ab) T.ψ)).re
+      ≤ ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
+          (if E ab.1 ab.2 then 4 * outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 else 0) :=
+        Finset.sum_le_sum fun ab _ => hterm ab
+    _ = 4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y E := by
+        rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, outcomeEventWeight, Finset.mul_sum]
+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
+        by_cases hE : E a b <;> simp [hE]
+
+/-- Formalization-only: expansion of a product of two local spectral
+combinations into the joint effects. -/
+theorem joint_expand (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
+    (u : G.AnswerA → ℂ) (v : G.AnswerB → ℂ) :
+    heteroKron (∑ a, u a • (T.A x).effect a) (∑ b, v b • (T.B y).effect b) =
+      ∑ a, ∑ b, (u a * v b) • heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b) := by
+  rw [heteroKron_sum_left]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+  rw [heteroKron_smul_left, heteroKron_sum_right, Finset.smul_sum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
+  rw [heteroKron_smul_right, smul_smul]
+
+/-- Formalization-only: the identity as a spectral combination of the effects of
+a measurement. -/
+theorem smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype d]
+    [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (s : ℂ) :
+    s • (1 : Op d) = ∑ a, s • M.effect a := by
+  rw [← Finset.smul_sum, M.sum_eq_one]
+
+end JointDefect
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

/-!
# Transfer of Bob's anticommutator estimate along the projective dilation

The right-placed counterpart of the Alice-side anticommutator transfer in
`Rigidity/Transfer.lean`: Bob's dilated observables leak out of the ground
slice by at most the forward cell-consistency defects, and the product of the
compressed observables is compared with the product of the dilated ones on the
dilated state through Alice's partner observable.

## References

`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

noncomputable section

/-- The norm of a difference acting on a state is symmetric. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_comm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) v‖ = ‖applyOperatorToState (N - M) v‖ := by
  rw [applyOperatorToState_sub_op, applyOperatorToState_sub_op, norm_sub_rev]

/-- Alice's dilated observable of a totalized bit, typed on the enlarged local
space.  Formalization-only abbreviation. -/
abbrev dilatedObsAf (S : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType) (f : MsAnswer → ZMod 2) :
    Op (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) :=
  obsOf (((msDilatedStrategy S).A x).postprocess f)

/-- The inflation of Bob's original observable is the ground compression of
his dilated observable. -/
theorem naimarkInflation_obs_B (S : Strategy msGame) (y : MsType) :
    naimarkInflation (α := MsAnswer) (obsOf ((S.B y).postprocess msBitOrZero)) =
      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * dilatedObsB S y msBitOrZero *
        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer := by
  change naimarkInflation (α := MsAnswer) (((S.B y).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect 0 -
    ((S.B y).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect 1) =
    groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
      (dilatedEffectB S y msBitOrZero 0 - dilatedEffectB S y msBitOrZero 1) *
      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer
  rw [naimarkInflation_sub, naimarkInflation_postprocess_B, naimarkInflation_postprocess_B,
    Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul]

/-- Alice's dilated totalized observables are contractions. -/
theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedObsAf (S : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType)
    (f : MsAnswer → ZMod 2) :
    (dilatedObsAf S x f)ᴴ * dilatedObsAf S x f ≤ 1 :=
  conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_obsOf _

/-- The leakage of Bob's dilated observable out of the ground slice is bounded
by the two forward intertwining defects of its effects. -/
theorem norm_leak_obs_le_B (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) *
        dilatedObsB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero))
        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ≤
      ‖applyOperatorToState
        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 0) 1 -
          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0))
        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
      ‖applyOperatorToState
        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 1) 1 -
          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1))
        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
  change ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) *
    (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0 -
      dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1)))
    (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ≤ _
  rw [Matrix.mul_sub, heteroKron_sub_right, applyOperatorToState_sub_op]
  refine le_trans (norm_sub_le _ _) (add_le_add ?_ ?_)
  · exact norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _
  · exact norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _

/-!
# Transfer of rigidity bounds along the projective dilation

The self-testing argument behind `thm:ms-rigidity` is carried out for the
projective dilation `msDilatedStrategy S` of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy
`S`.  Its conclusions are state-dependent bounds for the *dilated* projectors,
conjugated by local isometries `φ_A`, `φ_B` out of the enlarged local spaces.
The witness for the original strategy is obtained by composing these isometries
with the ground embeddings, and the operators appearing in its bounds are the
conjugates of the *original* effects, that is, of the compressions `Π P Π` of
the dilated projectors `P` to the ground slice (`Π` the ground projection).

Naimark dilation preserves Born probabilities but not state-dependent `≈_δ`
estimates in general (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`,
blueprint `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`), so `Π P Π` and `P` need not act
alike on the dilated state.  Their difference on the dilated state `ψ'` is the
*leakage* `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of `P` out of the ground slice, and the point of this
file is that in the Magic Square game this leakage is controlled by the
cell-consistency defect of the value-to-parity layer: the dilated effect
`P ⊗ 1` almost agrees with the partner effect `1 ⊗ Q` on the other side, and
`(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.  Combined with the closeness of
`(φ_A ⊗ φ_B) ψ'` to the ideal state and the fact that all operators involved
are contractions, this pulls every bound of `thm:ms-rigidity` back from the
dilated strategy to the original one with explicit constants.

## Main statements

* `ms_effect_transfer_A`, `ms_effect_transfer_B`: the bit-measurement distances
  of the original strategy are bounded by three times those of the dilated
  strategy plus `216 ε + 24 η²`, where `η` bounds the state closeness.
* `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`, `ms_anticommutator_transfer_B`: the
  anticommutator defects transfer with the bound `3 · (dilated) + 15552 ε +
  48 η²`.
* `ms_state_transfer`: the state closeness is unchanged.

## References

`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

noncomputable section

/-! ## Cell consistency of the postprocessed effects -/

/-- The Born overlap of Alice's totalized variable bit with Bob's totalized
constraint bit, summed over the bit, is the complement of the reverse
cell-mismatch mass. -/
theorem sum_stateQForm_reverse_eq (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    ∑ b : ZMod 2, stateQForm S.ψ (heteroKron
        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
      1 - reverseCellMismatchMass S i k := by
  classical
  have hterm : ∀ b : ZMod 2, stateQForm S.ψ (heteroKron
        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
      ∑ a : msGame.AnswerA, ∑ c : msGame.AnswerB,
        if msBitOrZero a = b then
          (if constraintBitOrZero k c = b then
            outcomeWeight S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i) a c else 0)
        else 0 := by
    intro b
    rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
      heteroKron_finset_sum_left, stateQForm_finset_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    split_ifs

/-!
# Magic Square value-to-parity relations

This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
six row or column constraints.

The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.

## References

The Magic Square game is defined in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:201-222`.  These relations are the
probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/

/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)

/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
theorem ms_support_subset_directed_incidences :
    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
  intro xy hxy
  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
  have heq' :
      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
          xy.swap :=
    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'

/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
theorem ms_support_card_le :
    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
  calc
    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
          directedIncidence).card :=
      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directed_incidences
    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
      Finset.card_image_le
    _ = 36 := by norm_num

/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩

/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩

/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by
  have hmemFilter :
      xy ∈ ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) := hxy
  rw [show (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy =
      1 / ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card : ℝ) by
    change (Distribution.uniformOnFinset
        ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
          Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges)).weight xy =
      1 / (((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges).card : ℝ)
    rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, if_pos hmemFilter]]
  apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le
  · exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨xy, hxy⟩
  · exact_mod_cast ms_support_card_le

/-! ## Rejection mass from the game value -/

/-- The rejection mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
noncomputable def rejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false

/-- The acceptance mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
noncomputable def acceptanceMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = true

/-- The rejection mass averaged over the Magic Square question distribution. -/
noncomputable def totalRejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) : ℝ :=
  avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2

/-- Acceptance and rejection partition the conditioned answer mass. -/
theorem acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
    acceptanceMass S x y + rejectionMass S x y = 1 := by
  rw [← show (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = 1 by
    exact outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one S x y]
  unfold acceptanceMass rejectionMass outcomeEventWeight
  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro a _
  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro b _
  cases h : msWinPredicate x y a b <;> simp [h]

/-!
# Contractions, isometries and the ground slice of the dilation

Support for the transfer step of `thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`):
the calculus needed to compare the dilated projective strategy of
`Rigidity/Dilation.lean` with the original strategy on states.

* Contractions: operators `K` with `Kᴴ K ≤ 1` do not increase norms; effects,
  observables of binary measurements, orthogonal projections, tensor placements,
  products and isometry conjugates are contractions.
* Matrices of isometries: `Vᴴ V = 1`, the two-sided isometry image of a state
  preserves norms, and a conjugated local operator acts on the transported state
  as the original operator acts on the original state.
* The ground projection `Π` of an enlarged local space: an orthogonal projection
  fixing the dilated state, with `Π P Π` the inflation of the compression of `P`.
* Leakage: the part `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of a dilated operator that leaves the ground
  slice is bounded by the intertwining defect of `P ⊗ 1` against any `1 ⊗ Q`,
  because `(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `(1 ⊗ Q) ψ'`.  This is the estimate that
  replaces the `≈_δ`-preservation which Naimark dilation lacks in general
  (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`, blueprint
  `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`).

## References

`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
-/

/-! ## Contractions and their action on states -/

/-- Applying a product of operators is successive application. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    applyOperatorToState (M * N) v =
      applyOperatorToState M (applyOperatorToState N v) := by
  unfold applyOperatorToState
  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same]

/-- The identity acts trivially. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    applyOperatorToState (1 : Op ι) v = v := by
  simp [applyOperatorToState]

/-- Operators act additively on states. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_add {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Op ι) (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    applyOperatorToState M (u + v) =
      applyOperatorToState M u + applyOperatorToState M v := by
  simp [applyOperatorToState]

/-- Operators act additively on differences of states. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_sub {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Op ι) (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    applyOperatorToState M (u - v) =
      applyOperatorToState M u - applyOperatorToState M v := by
  simp [applyOperatorToState]

/-- The action on states is additive in the operator. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_add_op {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    applyOperatorToState (M + N) v =
      applyOperatorToState M v + applyOperatorToState N v := by
  simp [applyOperatorToState]

/-- Operators annihilate the zero state. -/
theorem applyOperatorToState_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Op ι) :
    applyOperatorToState M (0 : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) = 0 := by
  simp [applyOperatorToState]

/-- Applying a product of rectangular matrices is successive application. -/
theorem toEuclideanLin_mul_apply {m n o : Type*} [Fintype n] [Fintype o]
    [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq o]
    (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (B : Matrix n o ℂ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ o) :
    Matrix.toEuclideanLin (A * B) v =
      Matrix.toEuclideanLin A (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B v) := by
  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same]

/-- The squared norm of `A v` is the quadratic form of `Aᴴ A` at `v`. -/
theorem norm_toEuclideanLin_sq {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) :
    ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v‖ ^ 2 =
      (inner ℂ v (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Aᴴ * A) v)).re := by
  rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ, Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
  change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v)).re =
    (inner ℂ v ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).adjoint (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v))).re
  rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]

/-- A rectangular matrix `A` with `Aᴴ A = 1` preserves norms. -/
theorem norm_toEuclideanLin_of_conjTranspose_mul_eq_one {m n : Type*} [Fintype m]
    [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℂ} (hA : Aᴴ * A = 1)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) :
    ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v‖ = ‖v‖ := by
  have h := norm_toEuclideanLin_sq A v
  have hv : (inner ℂ v v).re = ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
    simpa using inner_self_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) v
  have hone : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) v = v := by
    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin]
  rw [hA, hone, hv] at h
  exact (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).1 h

/-- The squared norm of `K v` is the quadratic form of `Kᴴ K` at `v`. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (K : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState K v‖ ^ 2 =
      (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState (Kᴴ * K) v)).re :=
  norm_toEuclideanLin_sq K v

/-- An operator `K` with `Kᴴ K ≤ 1` does not increase norms. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {K : Op ι} (hK : Kᴴ * K ≤ 1) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState K v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ := by
  have h := quadratic_form_mono hK v
  have hv : (inner ℂ v v).re = ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
    simpa using inner_self_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) v
  rw [← norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, applyOperatorToState_one, hv] at h
  exact (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).1 h

/-- The difference of two contractions at most doubles norms. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {A B : Op ι} (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hB : Bᴴ * B ≤ 1) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (A - B) v‖ ≤ 2 * ‖v‖ := by
  have hsplit : applyOperatorToState (A - B) v =
      applyOperatorToState A v - applyOperatorToState B v := by
    simp [applyOperatorToState]
  rw [hsplit]
  calc ‖applyOperatorToState A v - applyOperatorToState B v‖ ≤
        ‖applyOperatorToState A v‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState B v‖ := norm_sub_le _ _
    _ ≤ ‖v‖ + ‖v‖ := add_le_add (norm_applyOperatorToState_le hA v)
        (norm_applyOperatorToState_le hB v)
    _ = 2 * ‖v‖ := by ring

/-- Orthogonal projections are contractions. -/
theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {P : Op ι} (hP : IsProj P) : Pᴴ * P ≤ 1 := by
  have hstar : Pᴴ = P := by
    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]
    exact hP.isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
  rw [hstar, hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
  exact sub_nonneg.mp hP.one_sub.nonneg

/-- Products of contractions are contractions. -/
theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {A B : Op ι} (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hB : Bᴴ * B ≤ 1) :
    (A * B)ᴴ * (A * B) ≤ 1 := by
  have h1 : (1 - Aᴴ * A).PosSemidef := Matrix.le_iff.mp hA
  have h2 := h1.conjTranspose_mul_mul_same B
  have h3 : Bᴴ * (1 - Aᴴ * A) * B = Bᴴ * B - (A * B)ᴴ * (A * B) := by
    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
    noncomm_ring
  refine le_trans ?_ hB
  rw [Matrix.le_iff, ← h3]
  exact h2

/-- Effects of a measurement are contractions. -/
theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_effect {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ι) (a : α) :
    (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1 := by
  rw [measurement_effect_hermitian]
  exact le_trans (sq_le_self (M.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one M a))
    (measurement_effect_le_one M a)

   117	
   118	The paper states the Euclidean estimate at scale `sqrt ε` at lines 624--626
   119	and explains the norm conversion and local basis change at lines 650--652. One
   120	universal constant applies to every strategy and nonnegative error parameter. -/
   121	theorem exists_ms_rigidity :
   122	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →

     4	/-!
     5	# Reflections and the state-dependent metric on operators
     6	
     7	The self-testing argument for the Magic Square game manipulates `±1`-valued
     8	observables rather than positive operator valued measures.  This file records
     9	the algebra of such observables and the estimates that convert Born masses into
    10	operator bounds.
    11	
    12	Postprocessing a projective measurement along a binary relabelling of its
    13	answers produces a *reflection*, that is, a self-adjoint involution; two
    14	reflections coming from one and the same measurement commute, and their product
    15	is the reflection attached to the sum of the two relabellings.  The reflections
    16	of the source are the binary observables of the rest of the development, so this
    17	file uses `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` and its algebra, defined in
    18	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`, rather than a second predicate of
    19	its own.  Two operators are compared through the norm of the difference of their
    20	actions on a fixed state, which is the relation written `M ≈ N` in the source;
    21	this comparison is symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, and is unchanged
    22	by multiplication on the left by an isometric operator.  Finally, a real spectral combination of
    23	the joint effects of the two players has state-dependent norm controlled by the
    24	Born mass of the answer pairs carrying a nonzero coefficient; this is the step
    25	that turns each rejection mass of the value-to-parity layer into an operator
    26	estimate.
    27	
    28	## References
    29	
    30	The statements supported here are the operator relations in `thm:ms-rigidity`,
    31	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    33	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.
    34	-/

    48	/-- Formalization-only: the tensor placement commutes with adjoints. -/
    49	theorem heteroKron_conjTranspose {ιA ιB : Type} (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
    50	    (heteroKron M N)ᴴ = heteroKron Mᴴ Nᴴ := by
    51	  unfold heteroKron
    52	  exact Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker M N
    53	
    54	/-- Formalization-only: scalars pass through the first factor. -/
    55	theorem heteroKron_smul_left {ιA ιB : Type} (c : ℂ) (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
    56	    heteroKron (c • M) N = c • heteroKron M N := by
    57	  unfold heteroKron
    58	  exact Matrix.smul_kronecker c M N
    59	
    60	/-- Formalization-only: finite sums pass through the first factor. -/
    61	theorem heteroKron_sum_left {ιA ιB γ : Type} [Fintype γ]
    62	    (M : γ → Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
    63	    heteroKron (∑ c, M c) N = ∑ c, heteroKron (M c) N := by
    64	  ext p q
    65	  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.sum_mul]
    66	
    67	/-- Formalization-only: finite sums pass through the second factor. -/
    68	theorem heteroKron_sum_right {ιA ιB γ : Type} [Fintype γ]
    69	    (M : Op ιA) (N : γ → Op ιB) :
    70	    heteroKron M (∑ c, N c) = ∑ c, heteroKron M (N c) := by
    71	  ext p q
    72	  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.mul_sum]
    73	
    74	end Kron

    76	/-! ## The state-dependent norm -/
    77	
    78	section StateNorm
    79	
    80	variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    81	
    82	/-- Formalization-only: the action of an operator on a state is homogeneous. -/
    83	theorem applyOperatorToState_smul (c : ℂ) (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    84	    applyOperatorToState (c • M) ψ = c • applyOperatorToState M ψ := by
    85	  unfold applyOperatorToState
    86	  simp only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply]
    87	
    88	/-- Formalization-only: the zero operator annihilates every state; the
    89	companion `applyOperatorToState_zero` annihilates the zero state instead. -/
    90	theorem applyOperatorToState_zero_op (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    91	    applyOperatorToState (0 : Op ι) ψ = 0 := by
    92	  unfold applyOperatorToState
    93	  simp only [map_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]
    94	
    95	/-- Formalization-only: acting by a finite sum of operators is the sum of the
    96	actions. -/
    97	theorem applyOperatorToState_sum {γ : Type} [Fintype γ]
    98	    (M : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    99	    applyOperatorToState (∑ c, M c) ψ = ∑ c, applyOperatorToState (M c) ψ := by
   100	  unfold applyOperatorToState
   101	  simp only [map_sum, LinearMap.sum_apply]
   102	
   103	/-- An isometric operator preserves the norm of every state. -/
   104	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_of_isometry {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1)
   105	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ‖applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
   106	  have h : ‖applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ ^ 2 = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   107	    rw [norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, hU, @norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ,
   108	      applyOperatorToState_one]
   109	    rfl
   110	  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ := norm_nonneg _
   111	  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖ψ‖ := norm_nonneg _
   112	  nlinarith [h, h1, h2]
   113	
   114	/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator does not change the
   115	state-dependent norm. -/
   116	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1)
   117	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   118	    ‖applyOperatorToState (U * M) ψ‖ = ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ := by
   119	  rw [applyOperatorToState_mul, norm_applyOperatorToState_of_isometry hU]
   120	
   121	end StateNorm

   123	/-! ## Reflections -/
   124	
   125	/-- The *reflections* of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   126	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, are the self-adjoint involutions attached to
   127	two-outcome projective measurements, which are exactly the binary observables
   128	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` of
   129	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.  The Magic Square rigidity
   130	argument therefore uses that predicate and its algebra directly:
   131	`IsBinaryObservable.one`, `IsBinaryObservable.mul`,
   132	`IsBinaryObservable.isometry`, `isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one` and
   133	`isBinaryObservable_one_heteroKron`.
   134	
   135	This abbreviation carries the source's word for the predicate and exists only so
   136	that the stacked swap-isometry branch of issue #104, written before the two
   137	predicates were merged, still elaborates; delete it once that branch has
   138	landed. -/
   139	abbrev IsReflection {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (X : Op ι) : Prop :=
   140	  IsBinaryObservable X
   141	
   142	/-- Operators placed on the two tensor factors commute. -/
   143	theorem heteroKron_comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   144	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] (X : Op ιA) (Y : Op ιB) :
   145	    heteroKron X (1 : Op ιB) * heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) Y =
   146	      heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) Y * heteroKron X (1 : Op ιB) := by
   147	  rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one, one_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
   148	
   149	/-! ## State-dependent closeness -/
   150	
   151	/-- Two operators are *close within `δ` on `ψ`* when the state-dependent norm of
   152	their difference is at most `δ`.  This is the relation written `M ≈_δ N` in
   153	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   154	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   155	def CloseOn {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   156	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) (M N : Op ι) : Prop :=
   157	  ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   158	
   159	namespace CloseOn
   160	
   161	variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   162	variable {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ η : ℝ} {M N P U : Op ι}
   163	
   164	/-- Equal operators are close at every nonnegative scale. -/
   165	theorem of_eq (h : M = N) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) : CloseOn ψ δ M N := by
   166	  have hzero : applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ = 0 := by
   167	    rw [h, sub_self, applyOperatorToState_zero_op]
   168	  rw [CloseOn, hzero, norm_zero]
   169	  exact hδ
   170	
   171	/-- Closeness is symmetric. -/
   172	theorem symm (h : CloseOn ψ δ M N) : CloseOn ψ δ N M := by
   173	  have happ : applyOperatorToState (N - M) ψ = -applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ := by
   174	    rw [show N - M = -(M - N) by abel]
   175	    unfold applyOperatorToState
   176	    simp only [map_neg, LinearMap.neg_apply]
   177	  rw [CloseOn, happ, norm_neg]
   178	  exact h
   179	
   180	/-- Enlarging the scale preserves closeness. -/
   181	theorem mono (h : CloseOn ψ δ M N) (hδ : δ ≤ η) : CloseOn ψ η M N :=
   182	  le_trans h hδ
   183	
   184	/-- Closeness composes by the triangle inequality. -/
   185	theorem trans (h₁ : CloseOn ψ δ M N) (h₂ : CloseOn ψ η N P) :
   186	    CloseOn ψ (δ + η) M P := by
   187	  have hsplit : M - P = (M - N) + (N - P) := by abel
   188	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (M - P) ψ‖
   189	      = ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ + applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ := by
   190	        rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_add_op]
   191	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ :=
   192	        norm_add_le _ _
   193	    _ ≤ δ + η := add_le_add h₁ h₂
   194	
   195	/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator preserves closeness. -/
   196	theorem isometry_mul (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (h : CloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   197	    CloseOn ψ δ (U * M) (U * N) := by
   198	  have hsub : U * M - U * N = U * (M - N) := by noncomm_ring
   199	  rw [CloseOn, hsub, norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul hU]
   200	  exact h
   201	
   202	end CloseOn

   206	section SignObs
   207	
   208	variable {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   209	
   210	/-- The `±1`-valued observable attached to a measurement together with a binary
   211	relabelling of its answers: an answer labelled `0` carries the eigenvalue `1`
   212	and an answer labelled `1` carries the eigenvalue `-1`.  For the Magic Square

   214	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   215	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   216	noncomputable def signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (f : α → ZMod 2) : Op d :=
   217	  ∑ a, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a
   218	
   219	/-- The sign observable is the observable of the binary measurement obtained by
   220	relabelling the answers. -/

     3	/-!
     4	# The Magic Square cell relations on the dilated strategy
     5	
     6	Every question of the projectively dilated Magic Square strategy carries a
     7	complete projective measurement, so each binary relabelling of its answers
     8	produces a reflection.  Three reflections are attached to a constraint question,
     9	one for each cell of the row or column, and one reflection is attached to each
    10	variable question; the three reflections of a constraint commute exactly and
    11	their product, in any order, is the reflection of the sum of the three reported
    12	bits.  Reflections of the two players commute exactly.
    13	
    14	The value-to-parity relations are converted here into operator estimates on the
    15	dilated state, with explicit constants: the six row and column products are
    16	close to the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear equation, and the two
    17	reflections that the two players attach to a common cell are close to each
    18	other.  The two logical Pauli pairs are the reflections at the cells labelled by
    19	the paper's first and fifth variables.
    20	
    21	## References
    22	
    23	The statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    24	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    26	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.  The variable and
    27	constraint indices are zero-based, so the paper's first and fifth variables are
    28	the cells `0` and `4`.
    29	-/

    39	/-! ## Deviation of a sign observable from a comparison observable -/
    40	
    41	/-- The sign of a binary value is `1` or `-1`. -/
    42	theorem bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one (b : ZMod 2) : bitSign b = 1 ∨ bitSign b = -1 := by
    43	  rcases (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) b with h | h <;> rw [h]
    44	  · left
    45	    norm_num [bitSign]
    46	  · right
    47	    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one]
    48	
    49	/-- The sign is injective on binary values. -/
    50	theorem bit_sign_injective : Function.Injective bitSign := by
    51	  intro b c hbc
    52	  by_contra hne
    53	  rcases (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) b with hb | hb <;>
    54	    rcases (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) c with hc | hc
    55	  · exact hne (hb.trans hc.symm)
    56	  · rw [hb, hc] at hbc
    57	    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one] at hbc
    58	  · rw [hb, hc] at hbc
    59	    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one] at hbc
    60	  · exact hne (hb.trans hc.symm)
    61	
    62	section SignDefect
    63	
    64	variable {G : Game}
    65	
    66	/-- Two sign observables of the two players, placed on the composite space,
    67	differ in the state-dependent norm by at most twice the square root of the Born
    68	mass of the answer pairs on which the two labels disagree.  This is the estimate
    69	that turns every mass of the value-to-parity layer into an operator relation of
    70	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
    71	theorem norm_alice_sub_bob_signObs_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
    72	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
    73	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
    74	    (f : G.AnswerA → ZMod 2) (g : G.AnswerB → ZMod 2) :
    75	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) f) 1 -
    76	        heteroKron 1 (signObs (T.B y) g)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
    77	      4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y (fun a b => f a ≠ g b) := by
    78	  classical
    79	  have hAone : (1 : Op T.ιA) = ∑ a, (1 : ℂ) • (T.A x).effect a := by
    80	    simpa using smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.A x) (1 : ℂ)
    81	  have hBone : (1 : Op T.ιB) = ∑ b, (1 : ℂ) • (T.B y).effect b := by
    82	    simpa using smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.B y) (1 : ℂ)
    83	  have hexpand : heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) f) 1 - heteroKron 1 (signObs (T.B y) g) =
    84	      ∑ a, ∑ b, ((bitSign (f a) - bitSign (g b) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
    85	        heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b) := by
    86	    rw [signObs, signObs]
    87	    nth_rewrite 1 [hBone]
    88	    nth_rewrite 1 [hAone]
    89	    rw [joint_expand, joint_expand, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    90	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    91	    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    92	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    93	    rw [← sub_smul]
    94	    congr 1
    95	    push_cast
    96	    ring
    97	  rw [hexpand]
    98	  refine norm_apply_joint_defect_sq_le T x y hA hB
    99	    (fun a b => bitSign (f a) - bitSign (g b)) (fun a b => f a ≠ g b) ?_ ?_
   100	  · intro a b
   101	    rcases bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one (f a) with h1 | h1 <;>
   102	      rcases bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one (g b) with h2 | h2 <;>
   103	        simp only [h1, h2] <;> norm_num
   104	  · intro a b hab
   105	    rw [not_not] at hab
   106	    rw [hab, sub_self]
   107	
   108	/-- Alice's sign observable deviates from a constant sign by at most twice the
   109	square root of the mass of the answers carrying the other label. -/
   110	theorem norm_alice_signObs_sub_const_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   111	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
   112	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
   113	    (f : G.AnswerA → ZMod 2) (c : ZMod 2) :
   114	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) f) 1 -
   115	        ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB))) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   116	      4 * aliceEventWeight T x (fun a => f a ≠ c) := by
   117	  classical
   118	  have hconst : heteroKron (1 : Op T.ιA) (signObs (T.B y) (fun _ => c)) =
   119	      ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB)) := by
   120	    rw [signObs, ← smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.B y) (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ)),
   121	      heteroKron_smul_right, heteroKron_one_one]
   122	  have h := norm_alice_sub_bob_signObs_sq_le T x y hA hB f (fun _ => c)
   123	  rw [hconst] at h
   124	  refine le_trans h (le_of_eq ?_)
   125	  congr 1
   126	  exact outcome_event_weight_left_eq T x y (fun a => f a ≠ c)
   127	
   128	/-- Bob's sign observable deviates from a constant sign by at most twice the
   129	square root of the mass of the answers carrying the other label. -/
   130	theorem norm_bob_signObs_sub_const_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   131	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
   132	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
   133	    (g : G.AnswerB → ZMod 2) (c : ZMod 2) :
   134	    ‖applyOperatorToState (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB)) -
   135	        heteroKron 1 (signObs (T.B y) g)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   136	      4 * bobEventWeight T y (fun b => c ≠ g b) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  have hconst : heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) (fun _ => c)) (1 : Op T.ιB) =
   139	      ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB)) := by
   140	    rw [signObs, ← smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.A x) (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ)),
   141	      heteroKron_smul_left, heteroKron_one_one]
   142	  have h := norm_alice_sub_bob_signObs_sq_le T x y hA hB (fun _ => c) g
   143	  rw [hconst] at h
   144	  refine le_trans h (le_of_eq ?_)
   145	  congr 1
   146	  exact outcome_event_weight_right_eq T x y (fun b => c ≠ g b)
   147	
   148	end SignDefect

   150	/-! ## Comparison of Born masses with the game error -/
   151	
   152	/-- Formalization-only: a squared state-dependent bound by four times a mass
   153	which is itself bounded by `36 * ε` yields closeness at scale `12 * sqrt ε`. -/
   154	private theorem closeOn_of_sq_le {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   155	    {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {M N : Op ι} {m ε : ℝ}
   156	    (hsq : ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m) (hm0 : 0 ≤ m)
   157	    (hm : m ≤ 36 * ε) : CloseOn ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) M N := by
   158	  have hε : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε := by
   159	    have h36 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 36 * ε := le_trans hm0 hm
   160	    linarith
   161	  have hbound : ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) ^ 2 := by
   162	    have hsq' : (12 * Real.sqrt ε) ^ 2 = 144 * ε := by
   163	      rw [mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hε]
   164	      ring
   165	    rw [hsq']
   166	    linarith
   167	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖
   168	      = Real.sqrt (‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2) :=
   169	        (Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)).symm
   170	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt ((12 * Real.sqrt ε) ^ 2) := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hbound
   171	    _ = 12 * Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity)

   295	/-- The sum of the three answer bits reported for a constraint question, with
   296	malformed answers contributing zero. -/
   297	def constraintBitSum (a : MsAnswer) : ZMod 2 :=
   298	  constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a
   299	
   300	/-- An answer whose three reported bits do not sum to the prescribed parity is a
   301	parity failure in the sense of the value-to-parity layer. -/
   302	theorem constraintParityFailure_of_bitSum_ne (i : Fin 6) (a : MsAnswer)
   303	    (h : constraintBitSum a ≠ msParity i) : ConstraintParityFailure i a := by
   304	  cases a with
   305	  | bit γ => exact wrong_constraint_answer_implies_parity_failure i (MsAnswer.bit γ) rfl
   306	  | triple β =>
   307	      intro hprod
   308	      apply h
   309	      have hsum : bitSign (∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = bitSign (msParity i) := by
   310	        rw [bit_sign_sum_fin_three]
   311	        exact hprod
   312	      have hbit := bit_sign_injective hsum
   313	      rw [Fin.sum_univ_three] at hbit
   314	      exact hbit

   439	/-! ## Substitution inside a product -/
   440	
   441	/-- Replacing the left factor of a product costs the distance between the two
   442	factors plus twice the cost of replacing the right factor by an operator
   443	commuting with both.  This is the mechanism by which a state-dependent relation
   444	is used in the middle of a word: the tail is first moved to the other player,
   445	where it commutes with everything acting on the first player. -/
   446	theorem CloseOn.mul_left_subst {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   447	    {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ η : ℝ} {X X' K K' : Op ι}
   448	    (hXX' : CloseOn ψ δ X X') (hKK' : CloseOn ψ η K K')
   449	    (hX : Xᴴ * X = 1) (hX' : X'ᴴ * X' = 1) (hK' : K'ᴴ * K' = 1)
   450	    (hcX : X * K' = K' * X) (hcX' : X' * K' = K' * X') :
   451	    CloseOn ψ (η + δ + η) (X * K) (X' * K) := by
   452	  have h1 : CloseOn ψ η (X * K) (X * K') := CloseOn.isometry_mul hX hKK'
   453	  have h2 : CloseOn ψ δ (X * K') (X' * K') := by
   454	    change ‖applyOperatorToState (X * K' - X' * K') ψ‖ ≤ δ
   455	    rw [show X * K' - X' * K' = K' * X - K' * X' by rw [hcX, hcX']]
   456	    exact CloseOn.isometry_mul hK' hXX'
   457	  have h3 : CloseOn ψ η (X' * K') (X' * K) := CloseOn.isometry_mul hX' hKK'.symm
   458	  exact (h1.trans h2).trans h3
   459

   462	/-- The product of Alice's three cell reflections of a constraint question, in
   463	any order in which the three positions occur once each, is the reflection
   464	attached to the sum of the three reported bits. -/
   465	theorem msCellObsA_prod_of (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ : Fin 3)
   466	    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   467	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :
   468	    msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂ =
   469	      heteroKron (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))
   470	        constraintBitSum) 1 := by
   471	  have hkey : signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))
   472	        (constraintBitOrZero k₀) *
   473	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i)) (constraintBitOrZero k₁) *
   474	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i)) (constraintBitOrZero k₂) =
   475	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i)) constraintBitSum := by
   476	    rw [signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _),
   477	      signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _)]
   478	    congr 1
   479	    funext a
   480	    exact hsum a
   481	  rw [msCellObsA, msCellObsA, msCellObsA, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul]
   482	  simp only [mul_one]
   483	  rw [hkey]

   486	order in which the three positions occur once each, is the reflection attached
   487	to the sum of the three reported bits. -/

   489	    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   490	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :
   491	    msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ =
   492	      heteroKron 1 (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).B (MsType.constraint i))
   493	        constraintBitSum) := by
   494	  have hkey : signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).B (MsType.constraint i))
   495	        (constraintBitOrZero k₀) *
   496	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).B (MsType.constraint i)) (constraintBitOrZero k₁) *
   497	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).B (MsType.constraint i)) (constraintBitOrZero k₂) =
   498	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).B (MsType.constraint i)) constraintBitSum := by
   499	    rw [signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_B S _),
   500	      signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_B S _)]
   501	    congr 1
   502	    funext a
   503	    exact hsum a
   504	  rw [msCellObsB, msCellObsB, msCellObsB, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul]
   505	  simp only [mul_one]
   506	  rw [hkey]

   508	/-- Each permuted row or column product of Alice's cell reflections is close, on
   509	the dilated state, to the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear
   510	equation. -/
   511	theorem msCellObsA_prod_close_of (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
   512	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (i : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ : Fin 3)
   513	    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   514	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :

   516	      (msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂)
   517	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • 1) := by
   518	  rw [msCellObsA_prod_of S i k₀ k₁ k₂ hsum, ← msCellObsA_prod S i]
   519	  exact msCellObsA_prod_close S ε hwin i

221	theorem signObs_eq_obsOf_postprocess (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   222	    (f : α → ZMod 2) : signObs M f = obsOf (M.postprocess f) := by
   223	  classical
   224	  have hcases : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1 := by decide
   225	  have key : ∀ a : α, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a =
   226	      (if f a = 0 then M.effect a else 0) - (if f a = 1 then M.effect a else 0) := by
   227	    intro a
   228	    rcases hcases (f a) with h | h <;> rw [h] <;>
   229	      norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one, neg_one_smul]
   230	  rw [signObs, obsOf, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   231	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter,
   232	    Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   233	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a

   236	/-- Formalization-only: the effects of a projective measurement are mutually
   237	orthogonal, so two spectral combinations of them multiply coefficientwise. -/
   238	private theorem sum_smul_effect_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   239	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c e : α → ℂ) :
   240	    (∑ a, c a • M.effect a) * (∑ a, e a • M.effect a) =
   241	      ∑ a, (c a * e a) • M.effect a := by
   242	  classical
   243	  have horth : ∀ a b : α, a ≠ b → M.effect a * M.effect b = 0 := fun a b hab =>
   244	    mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hM M.sum_le_one hab
   245	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   246	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   247	  have hidem : M.effect a * M.effect a = M.effect a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem
   248	  rw [Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.smul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
   249	  · rw [Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hidem]
   250	  · intro b _ hba
   251	    rw [Matrix.mul_smul, horth a b (Ne.symm hba), smul_zero, smul_zero]
   252	  · intro ha
   253	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha

   256	/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement multiply by adding their
   257	relabellings. -/
   258	theorem signObs_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   259	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
   260	    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M (fun a => f a + g a) := by
   261	  rw [signObs, signObs, sum_smul_effect_mul M hM, signObs]
   262	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   263	  rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← bit_sign_add]

   265	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   266	/-- The sign observable of the zero relabelling is the identity. -/
   267	theorem signObs_const_zero (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   268	    signObs M (fun _ => 0) = 1 := by
   269	  have hb : ((bitSign (0 : ZMod 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by norm_num [bitSign]
   270	  rw [signObs]
   271	  simp only [hb, one_smul]
   272	  exact M.sum_eq_one

   274	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   275	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is an involution. -/
   276	theorem signObs_mul_self (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   277	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   278	    signObs M f * signObs M f = 1 := by
   279	  rw [signObs_mul M hM]
   280	  have hzero : (fun a => f a + f a) = fun _ : α => (0 : ZMod 2) := by
   281	    funext a
   282	    exact (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x + x = 0) (f a)
   283	  rw [hzero, signObs_const_zero]

   288	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   289	    (signObs M f)ᴴ = signObs M f := by
   290	  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, signObs, star_sum]
   291	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   292	  rw [star_smul]
   293	  congr 1
   294	  · simp
   295	  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint

   300	theorem isBinaryObservable_signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   301	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :

   303	  ⟨signObs_conjTranspose M hM f, signObs_mul_self M hM f⟩

   308	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
   309	    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M g * signObs M f := by
   310	  rw [signObs_mul M hM, signObs_mul M hM]
   311	  congr 1
   312	  funext a

   321	/-- Formalization-only: scalars pass through the second tensor factor. -/
   322	theorem heteroKron_smul_right {ιA ιB : Type} (c : ℂ) (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
   323	    heteroKron M (c • N) = c • heteroKron M N := by
   324	  unfold heteroKron
   325	  exact Matrix.kronecker_smul c M N

   327	/-- Formalization-only: the tensor placement of two orthogonal projections is an
   328	orthogonal projection. -/
   329	private theorem isProj_heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   330	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {A : Op ιA} {B : Op ιB}
   331	    (hA : IsProj A) (hB : IsProj B) : IsProj (heteroKron A B) := by
   332	  have hAi : A * A = A := hA.isIdempotentElem
   333	  have hBi : B * B = B := hB.isIdempotentElem
   334	  have hAs : Aᴴ = A := by
   335	    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]; exact hA.isSelfAdjoint
   336	  have hBs : Bᴴ = B := by
   337	    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]; exact hB.isSelfAdjoint
   338	  constructor
   339	  · change heteroKron A B * heteroKron A B = heteroKron A B
   340	    rw [heteroKron_mul, hAi, hBi]
   341	  · change star (heteroKron A B) = heteroKron A B
   342	    rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, heteroKron_conjTranspose, hAs, hBs]
   343	
   344	/-- Formalization-only: a real spectral combination of the effects of a
   345	projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
   346	private theorem sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose {α d : Type} [Fintype α]
   347	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   348	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c : α → ℝ) :
   349	    (∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a)ᴴ = ∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a := by
   350	  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_sum]
   351	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   352	  rw [star_smul]
   353	  congr 1
   354	  · simp
   355	  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint

   357	/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a real spectral combination on a
   358	state is the corresponding real combination of the individual quadratic
   359	forms. -/
   360	private theorem re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul {ι γ : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   361	    [Fintype γ] (r : γ → ℝ) (K : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   362	    (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (∑ c, ((r c : ℝ) : ℂ) • K c) ψ)).re =
   363	      ∑ c, r c * (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (K c) ψ)).re := by
   364	  rw [applyOperatorToState_sum, inner_sum, Complex.re_sum]
   365	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_
   366	  rw [applyOperatorToState_smul, inner_smul_right]
   367	  simp

   371	/-- Formalization-only: the joint effects of the two players form a projective
   372	measurement on the composite space when both local measurements are
   373	projective. -/
   374	private noncomputable def jointMeasurement (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   375	    (y : G.QuestionB) :
   376	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) (T.ιA × T.ιB) :=
   377	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   378	    (fun ab => heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2))
   379	    (fun ab => kronecker_nonneg ((T.A x).pos ab.1) ((T.B y).pos ab.2))
   380	    (by
   381	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   382	      calc ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   383	            heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)
   384	          = ∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a)
   385	              (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (T.B y).effect b) := by
   386	            exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (heteroKron_sum_right _ _).symm
   387	        _ = heteroKron (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (T.A x).effect a) (1 : Op T.ιB) := by
   388	            rw [(T.B y).sum_eq_one, heteroKron_sum_left]
   389	        _ = 1 := by rw [(T.A x).sum_eq_one, heteroKron_one_one])
   390	
   391	/-- Formalization-only: the effects of the joint measurement. -/
   392	private theorem jointMeasurement_effect (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   393	    (y : G.QuestionB) (ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) :
   394	    (jointMeasurement T x y).effect ab =
   395	      heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2) := rfl
   396	
   397	/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a joint effect is the Born weight
   398	of the corresponding answer pair. -/
   399	private theorem re_inner_jointMeasurement_effect (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   400	    (y : G.QuestionB) (ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) :
   401	    (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState ((jointMeasurement T x y).effect ab) T.ψ)).re =
   402	      outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 := rfl
   403	
   404	/-- A real spectral combination of the joint effects deviates from zero, in the
   405	state-dependent norm, by at most the mass of the answer pairs carrying a nonzero
   406	coefficient, scaled by the squared coefficient bound.  This is the estimate that
   407	converts each Magic Square rejection mass into an operator bound;
   408	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   409	theorem norm_apply_joint_defect_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   410	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
   411	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
   412	    (coef : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → ℝ) (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop)
   413	    [DecidableRel E] (hbound : ∀ a b, coef a b ^ 2 ≤ 4)
   414	    (hsupp : ∀ a b, ¬ E a b → coef a b = 0) :
   415	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   416	        (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, ((coef a b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
   417	          heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   418	      4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y E := by
   419	  classical
   420	  set J := jointMeasurement T x y with hJ
   421	  have hJproj : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective J := fun ab =>
   422	    isProj_heteroKron (hA ab.1) (hB ab.2)
   423	  have hcollapse : (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, ((coef a b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
   424	      heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)) =
   425	      ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab := by
   426	    rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   427	    rfl
   428	  have hsa : (∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab)ᴴ =
   429	      ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab :=
   430	    sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose J hJproj (fun ab => coef ab.1 ab.2)
   431	  have hsq : ∀ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
   432	      ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) =
   433	        ((coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
   434	    intro ab
   435	    rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, sq]
   436	  rw [hcollapse, norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, hsa,
   437	    sum_smul_effect_mul J hJproj]
   438	  simp only [hsq]
   439	  rw [re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul]
   440	  have hterm : ∀ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
   441	      coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 *
   442	          (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState (J.effect ab) T.ψ)).re ≤
   443	        (if E ab.1 ab.2 then 4 * outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 else 0) := by
   444	    intro ab
   445	    have hw : 0 ≤ outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 := outcomeWeight_nonneg T x y ab.1 ab.2
   446	    rw [re_inner_jointMeasurement_effect]
   447	    by_cases hE : E ab.1 ab.2
   448	    · rw [if_pos hE]
   449	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hbound ab.1 ab.2) hw
   450	    · rw [if_neg hE, hsupp ab.1 ab.2 hE]
   451	      simp
   452	  calc ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 *
   453	        (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState (J.effect ab) T.ψ)).re
   454	      ≤ ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
   455	          (if E ab.1 ab.2 then 4 * outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 else 0) :=
   456	        Finset.sum_le_sum fun ab _ => hterm ab
   457	    _ = 4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y E := by
   458	        rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, outcomeEventWeight, Finset.mul_sum]
   459	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   460	        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   461	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   462	        by_cases hE : E a b <;> simp [hE]
   463	
   464	/-- Formalization-only: expansion of a product of two local spectral
   465	combinations into the joint effects. -/
   466	theorem joint_expand (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   467	    (u : G.AnswerA → ℂ) (v : G.AnswerB → ℂ) :
   468	    heteroKron (∑ a, u a • (T.A x).effect a) (∑ b, v b • (T.B y).effect b) =
   469	      ∑ a, ∑ b, (u a * v b) • heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b) := by
   470	  rw [heteroKron_sum_left]
   471	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   472	  rw [heteroKron_smul_left, heteroKron_sum_right, Finset.smul_sum]
   473	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   474	  rw [heteroKron_smul_right, smul_smul]

   478	theorem smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype d]
   479	    [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (s : ℂ) :
   480	    s • (1 : Op d) = ∑ a, s • M.effect a := by

   626	    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_smul, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]
   627	    congr 1
   628	    simp
   629	  rw [hstar, Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hU,
   630	    bitSign_ofReal_mul_self, one_smul]
   631	
   632	/-! ## Building blocks of the solution-group computation -/

   634	/-- One of Bob's three cell reflections of a constraint question is close, on
   635	the dilated state, to the signed product of the other two. -/
   636	theorem msCellObsB_single_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   637	    (i : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ : Fin 3)
   638	    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   639	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :
   640	    CloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsB S i k₁)
   641	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
   642	        (msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₂)) := by
   643	  have hprod := msCellObsB_prod_close_of S ε hwin i k₀ k₁ k₂ hsum
   644	  have hX2 : msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₀ = 1 :=
   645	    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₀).mul_self_eq_one
   646	  have hZ2 : msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₂ = 1 :=
   647	    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₂).mul_self_eq_one
   648	  have hZY : msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₁ =
   649	      msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := msCellObsB_comm S i k₂ k₁
   650	  have hZX : msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀ =
   651	      msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := msCellObsB_comm S i k₂ k₀
   652	  have hU : (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀)ᴴ *
   653	      (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) = 1 :=
   654	    ((isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₂).mul
   655	      (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₀) hZX).isometry
   656	  have e1 : (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) *

   658	    calc (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) *

   660	        = msCellObsB S i k₂ *
   661	            ((msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₀) * msCellObsB S i k₁) *
   662	            msCellObsB S i k₂ := by noncomm_ring
   663	      _ = msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := by
   664	          rw [hX2, one_mul]
   665	      _ = msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := by rw [hZY]
   666	      _ = msCellObsB S i k₁ := by rw [mul_assoc, hZ2, mul_one]

   668	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op _)) =
   669	      ((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₂) := by
